definition: The METEO System is a machine translation system specifically designed for the translation of the weather forecasts issued daily by Environment Canada.
details: The system was used from 1981 to 30 September 2001 by Environment Canada to translate forecasts issued in French in the province of Quebec into English and those issued in English in other Canadian provinces into French. Since then, a competitor program has replaced METEO System after an open governmental bid. The system was developed by John Chandioux and was often mentioned as one of the few success stories in the field of machine translation.
story: Think of a grammar teacher who never memorized a rule but can still tell you when a sentence sounds wrong. Think of it this way: The METEO System is a machine translation system specifically designed for the translation of the weather forecasts issued daily by Environment Canada. And here is the clever part: The system was used from 1981 to 30 September 2001 by Environment Canada to translate forecasts issued in French in the province of Quebec into English and those issued in English in other Canadian provinces into French. The machine learns to read between the lines by reading an impossible number of lines. And that is METEO System — teaching a machine to read between the lines.
